standard_prerequisites.name: Circle code and its two maps
standard_prerequisites.statement: The code family assigns types to the points of the circle, encode transports the canonical element along a path, and decode reads an element of the code as a path to the base point.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two maps composed in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Path induction
standard_prerequisites.statement: To prove a statement about an arbitrary path from a fixed point it suffices to prove it for the reflexivity path.
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the claim to the base point.

standard_prerequisites.name: Computation of the two maps at the base point
standard_prerequisites.statement: Encoding the reflexivity path at the base point is the integer zero, and decoding zero at the base point is the reflexivity path.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two judgemental computations that close the proof.

core_obligations: Reduce the claim to the base point and the reflexivity path by path induction (source lines 582-583).
Compute the encoding of the reflexivity path at the base point as transport of the canonical integer along reflexivity, which is the integer zero by definition (source lines 584-586).
Compute the decoding of zero at the base point as the zeroth power of the generating loop, which is the reflexivity path by definition, closing the argument (source lines 586-587).

proof_roadmap.step: Path induction: only the base point and the reflexivity path remain.
Two definitional computations close the case.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 576-579 (book Lemma 8.1.7): for every point x of the circle and every path p from the base point to x, decoding the encoding of p returns p. The statement is an identity between composites over an arbitrary point, and the proof (source lines 580-587) first uses path induction to reduce it to the reflexivity path at the base point, where the two composites have to be unfolded by definition: encoding reflexivity is transport of the canonical integer along reflexivity, hence zero, and decoding zero is the zeroth power of the generating loop, hence reflexivity. Which definitions have to be unfolded, and why the general case needs no further argument, is the content and the statement shows none of it.
